mod-description: Gear-driven workshop machines and limited automation.
handbook-text-pneumatic-router:
Joins up to four tube lines. Mount its base on a floor, wall or ceiling. Connected pipes determine input and output directions. Air from the strongest input is shared between the outputs; more branches need more air.

Empty-hand right-click opens the editor. Sneak and right-click with a placeable item also opens it. Count the brass marks on the connections: they match buttons 1–4. Select a port to highlight it on the machine. Choose an output, edit its settings, then press Apply.

Each output has up to eight filters. An output without filters accepts any supported item. Use Choose inventory sample to pick from your hotbar or backpack without using the item. All include rules must match unless Any include is enabled. Exclude always blocks its matches. Inputs have no filters.

Within a rule, AND runs before OR; optional parentheses change the grouping. Material samples start with all tags joined by OR, such as (block:metal OR metal:copper). Edit the list or choose a single tag.

Priority 3 is highest, 1 lowest. Round robin alternates equal-priority routes to the requesting Receiver and skips busy routes; Forced round robin waits for its chosen route. Packages keep their intended chest. A flashing upper gear means a package is held; fix the route or filters. The router checks again once per second.

Transit takes one second with enough air. Items enter and leave at tube speed, pausing for the table to turn. Busy routers queue packages. Wrench right-click rotates the ports; sneak-wrench changes the mounting face. Wait until empty with no approaching package.
pneumatic-help-router-place: Attach base to a surface; marks show the four tube faces
router-physical-ports: Count the brass marks on the ports. Select one to highlight it on the machine.
router-port-info: Air inlet mark: {0}. Connected outlets: {1}. Empty-hand or sneak right-click to configure.
router-forced-round-robin: Forced round robin / wait for turn
router-policy-help: Priority 3 is highest. All routes lead to the Receiver requesting the items.
router-input-help: This pipe supplies the router. To filter deliveries, select an output.
router-expression-help: Values: AND first, then OR. ( ) optional.
router-expression-invalid: Check values, AND/OR and matching parentheses.
router-expression-limit: Too many filter values. Shorten the lists and try again.
router-filter-help-identity: Choose an inventory sample to match only that type and variant, or enter its full mod:code.
router-filter-help-mod: Choose a sample to include items and blocks from its mod, or enter the mod ID.
router-filter-help-item: Matches items rather than placeable blocks. No value is needed.
router-filter-help-block: Matches placeable blocks. No value is needed.
router-filter-help-material: Samples join their tags with OR. Choose one tag, or use AND to require several.
router-filter-help-tool: Sample a tool or enter its tool type, e.g. Pickaxe. Empty means any tool.
router-filter-help-food: Matches food that can be transported. Perishable goods cannot travel. No value needed.
router-filter-help-fuel: Matches goods that can burn as fuel. No value is needed.
router-filter-help-smeltable: Matches goods that can be smelted. No value is needed.
router-filter-help-stackable: Matches items that stack. No value is needed.
router-filter-help-durability: Minimum remaining durability, 0–100%. For tools below 50%, include Tool type and exclude this rule at 50.
router-filter-help-code: Enter a mod:code pattern. * matches any text; ? matches one character.
router-filter-help-attribute: Advanced: require a named property on the item or its type.
pneumatic-status-filtered: Cargo held; check the outgoing pipes and router filters.
pneumatic-status-router-preparing: Waiting for the carriage to dock.
pneumatic-status-lost: Holding cargo; retrying a route to its original receiver.
pneumatic-status-config-stale: Settings changed while this editor was open. Reopen it and apply again.
handbook-text-pneumatic-tube:
Connect a Pneumatic Accumulator to a Sender supplied by an ordinary single wooden chest. Run glass tubes to a Receiver and destination chest. Lightly tinted glass lets you follow packages through the line. A tube, Sender or Receiver outlet pointing directly into a chest also receives automatically.

Look to aim the outlet, including up or down. It points opposite your view normally; hold sneak to point it along your view. When joining an existing outlet, your aim chooses the new exit and can form an elbow. Follow the placement arrows.

Wrench right-click changes the outlet. Sneak-wrench swaps input and output. Blue specks show airflow. Full chests, busy sections, weak air and broken connections make items wait. Keep the route and both chests loaded. Breaking an occupied section drops its items.
handbook-text-pneumatic-sender:
Draws solid items and tools from an ordinary single wooden chest on its branch. Connect the input to a Pneumatic Accumulator and the output to glass tubes. A downstream receiving chest requests batches of up to eight when it has room; stocking a Sender alone does not start delivery. Router filters choose which goods can be requested.

Place in two clicks: aim the tube direction and right-click, release, then look to aim the chest branch and right-click again. Follow the purple arrow. Both stages point opposite your view normally; hold sneak to point along it. The branch must be perpendicular to the tube. Ctrl and right-click cancels.

Wrench right-click changes the tube direction; sneak-wrench changes the chest branch. Wait for deliveries to finish before redirecting it. Empty-hand right-click shows status. Its main outlet can also receive into a chest. Tools keep their durability; liquid containers and perishable goods cannot travel.
handbook-text-pneumatic-receiver:
Requests batches of up to eight items from connected Senders when its branch chest has room. Use an ordinary single wooden chest. Packages for a later Receiver pass through. Its main outlet also receives when aimed directly into a chest; the two chests take turns when both have room.

Place in two clicks: aim the tube direction and right-click, release, then look to aim the chest branch and right-click again. Follow the purple arrow. Both stages point opposite your view normally; hold sneak to point along it. The branch must be perpendicular to the tube. Ctrl and right-click cancels.

Wrench right-click changes the tube direction; sneak-wrench changes the chest branch. Wait for deliveries to finish before redirecting it. Empty-hand right-click shows status. A full destination makes its package wait. Replacing that chest blocks the old delivery; break the section holding it to recover the items.
handbook-text-pneumatic-accumulator:
Stores air from up to three Automatic Bellows to power item transport. Place it upright. Point the bellows' nozzles into its three small sockets, and connect the large glass outlet to a Sender or pneumatic tube. Wrench right-click rotates the outlet.

The leather reservoir rises as it fills. Three bellows driven from below at one revolution per second settle around half full. Faster shafts build a fuller reserve and supply longer lines. A full reservoir releases air four times as fast as a half-full one. When the bellows stop, stored air keeps the line running briefly and weakens as it empties.

Blue specks show airflow from the outlet. Longer routes, more moving batches and router branches need more air. Keep the route and both chests loaded. Only the bellows needs a driven shaft; the Accumulator needs no axle or fuel.
pneumatic-help-place: Aim opposite your view; hold sneak to aim along it
pneumatic-help-two-click: Aim tube direction, then inventory direction; sneak reverses either stage
pneumatic-place-failed: Cannot place at the selected position. Check space and access, then select it again.
pneumatic-rotate-busy: Wait for the current delivery and mechanism to finish before redirecting this machine.
pneumatic-inventory-below: Inventory branch: ordinary wooden chest directly below.
pneumatic-inventory-direction: Inventory branch: {0}; attach an ordinary single wooden chest on that face.
pneumatic-outlet-receiving: Main outlet receives into the chest to the {0}.
pneumatic-status-ordered: A batch is on its way.
pneumatic-status-no-inventory: No ordinary single wooden chest connected at the destination.
pneumatic-status-inventory-changed: Cargo held; its original destination chest has been replaced.
pneumatic-status-no-offer: No available goods on the powered upstream route.
pneumatic-status-destination-full: Destination full; cargo is held here.
pneumatic-status-occupied: Waiting for the next section to clear.
pneumatic-status-route-broken: Cargo held; restore its original pipe connections.
pneumatic-status-protected-route: Current inventory or land permissions prevent this transfer.
pneumatic-status-network-limit: Too many loaded pneumatic parts; reduce the connected equipment.
pneumatic-status-save-paused: Transport paused after a save error. Check the server log before restarting.
pneumatic-status-protected-state: Transport paused: this machine's save data needs recovery or a newer Gearwright version.
handbook-text-large-bellows:
Supplies air to a burning forge or a Pneumatic Accumulator. Point its nozzle directly into the forge or an accumulator socket. Place a Reciprocating Drive Shaft one block below its rear half, with the axle crossing the bellows' width, and supply mechanical power.

A shaft one block above the rear half can drive the top board instead. If both shafts are present, the lower one takes priority even when stopped. Remove it to use the upper shaft. Either rotation direction works.

Driving from below gives a steady supply that continues briefly after stopping. Driving from above gives pulses and slightly more air per revolution. Faster shafts supply more air. Three bellows driven from below at one revolution per second hold an accumulator around half full.

In creative mode, find Automatic Bellow in the Gearwright tab.
bellows-readonly: Bellows drive disabled: saved data needs recovery or a newer Gearwright version.
bellows-unconnected: No shaft crank connected. Place one above or below the rear half, across the bellows' width.
bellows-bottom: Connected to the lower shaft crank. Stored air smooths delivery.
bellows-top: Connected to the upper shaft crank. The top board delivers air in pulses.
handbook-text-fluid-pipe-copper:
Carries liquid or steam through connected ports. Full pipes can carry flow through a connected outlet. Longer runs and uphill routes reduce delivery; use a shorter supply line or more pump pressure for faster flow. Gravity moves liquid downhill; a pump can lift it against gravity. Blocked lines retain liquid and build pressure. Steam compresses much more easily and flows by pressure without water-column weight. Place it against the face it should connect to; sneak while placing to open the opposite face instead. Use a wrench on a face to open or close that port.

rightmouse a free face with plain glass, a Steel Sprinkler (bottom face only), a Copper Pipe Nozzle (any face), or a copper plate (an open port facing air). Glass makes a lightly tinted window onto the contents. Sneak and rightmouse with an empty hand to remove a fitting.

rightmouse with one plank to fit a wooden frame. Frames join neighboring frames without gaps, with collars around pipe ends and one diagonal brace on each empty side and bottom. The sparse top supports a barrel whenever there is no pipe above. An upward connection leaves a gap for the barrel nozzle.

Add one more plank to insulate the frame with crate panels. The insulated pipe counts as a full block for rooms and attachments and blocks daylight. Pipe connections and fittings still work; the panels cover inspection windows. An open frame alone does not seal a room. Sneak and rightmouse with an empty hand to recover the lining plank first, then click the wood to recover the frame plank. Breaking the pipe returns both installed planks and its fittings in survival.

Creative mode: find it in the Gearwright tab.
handbook-text-creative-fluid-pump:
Creative-only source for a connected Copper Pipe. rightmouse to choose liquid or steam and set 0-1000 kPa; 0 stops the source. Lightly tinted glass covers the front dial.

Find it in the Gearwright creative tab.
handbook-text-passive-fluid-pump: Legacy block with no current function. Use a Copper Pipe Nozzle to connect a pipe to an unsealed liquid container.
handbook-text-sprinkler-brass:
rightmouse the bottom face of a Copper Pipe to attach it. Water reaches farmland one to four blocks below; higher pressure increases its circular reach from one to four blocks. Steam will not pass through it, and other liquids kill affected crops.

Creative mode: find it in the Gearwright tab.
handbook-text-irrigator-pipe-bronze:
Place in a straight horizontal run below solid ceiling blocks; it follows the direction you face and connects at its ends. It waters the first farmland one to four blocks below its three outlets, up to 80% moisture. Steam will not irrigate, and other liquids kill affected crops. See the Copper Pipe for a configurable supply line.

Creative mode: find it in the Gearwright tab.
handbook-text-fluid-pipe-intake-copper:
rightmouse a free face of a Copper Pipe to attach it. It transfers liquid to or from an adjacent unsealed container.

Point it into a full natural liquid source block and use a Reciprocating Pump to draw liquid without draining the source. Extraction requires at least 70 kPa of suction (-70 kPa gauge pressure). Keep the intake short and avoid large lifts for better filling.

A nozzle pointing sideways or down into open air drains liquid away; one pointing up releases overflow only. Sneak and rightmouse with an empty hand to remove it.

Creative mode: find it in the Gearwright tab.
handbook-text-pottery-profile-tool: Creative-only item with no gameplay action. Find it in the Gearwright creative tab.
handbook-text-small-flywheel:
Place inline with a horizontal Wooden Axle; leave a clear space 3 blocks wide, 3 high and 1 thick around its shaft. The flywheel stores momentum as it speeds up and helps the machinery coast when power falls. It cannot power a sustained overload, and each flywheel adds friction. Look at it to see its speed in rpm.

Creative mode: find it in the Gearwright tab.
handbook-text-overrunning-transmission:
Place inline by clicking the source-side axle; that side becomes the input. The ratchet drives the output while the input is faster, then freewheels when the output overtakes it. Use it to keep an unreliable power source from slowing a shared workshop shaft. It works in either rotation direction. Break and replace it from the other end to swap input and output.

It stores no power. Add a Small Flywheel if the workshop needs to coast through interruptions.

Creative mode: find it in the Gearwright tab.
handbook-text-lateral-crank:
Place inline with a horizontal Wooden Axle. Attach up to four devices, one on each face around the shaft. Reciprocating Pumps connect beside it; Automatic Bellow connects above or below it at the bellow's rear half, with the shaft crossing its width. Automatic Bellow uses only one shaft and prefers an aligned shaft below it.

All devices share the shaft's power; a blocked pump can slow or stop the others. With no device attached, rightmouse with an empty hand to turn the journal by 45 degrees. Use this to stagger strokes along separate drive shafts. Remove all attached devices before changing the angle.

Creative mode: find it in the Gearwright tab.
handbook-text-reciprocating-pump:
Place beside a Reciprocating Drive Shaft, or place the pump first and add the shaft against its drive face. The copper-rimmed connection is the input; the bronze-rimmed connection is the output. Sneak while placing to swap them. Up to four pumps can share one shaft.

The upstroke draws liquid into the 4 L chamber; the downstroke pushes it into the output pipe. Delivery pauses between strokes. Lightly tinted glass covers both chamber windows; watch the liquid level and piston through them. The tooltip also shows how much is inside. Steam and all liquids accepted by liquid containers are supported.

A blocked outlet raises pressure and can slow, stop or push back the shaft, including other pumps on it. Open a path for the output to drain. The 1500 kPa service rating can be exceeded; it is not an automatic pressure release.

To draw from a natural source, fit a Copper Pipe Nozzle to the input line and point it into a full source block. The pump slows its upstroke to help the chamber fill. Dry pipes take time to prime. If filling is poor, shorten the intake, reduce the lift or slow the drive. An elevated container or another pump can improve supply.

Creative mode: find it in the Gearwright tab.
handbook-text-controlled-clutch: Use an adjacent Clutch to engage or disengage this transmission. Engaging it brings the two shafts toward the same speed. Disengaging it separates their drive, so machinery on either side can coast or keep turning under its own power.
flywheel-state-read-only: The flywheel cannot read its saved data. Operation is paused to protect it.
controlled-clutch-waiting: Waiting for a mechanical network on both shaft ends.
controlled-clutch-bypassed: Both ends are already joined by another mechanical path.
lateral-crank-angle-locked: Remove all attached devices before changing the drive phase.
lateral-crank-state-read-only: The shaft cannot read its saved data. Its angle setting cannot be changed.
reciprocating-pump-status-disconnected: The reciprocating drive shaft is disconnected.
reciprocating-pump-status-dead-center: Piston is at a dead centre.
reciprocating-pump-status-output-blocked: The output pipe is disconnected or blocked.
reciprocating-pump-status-output-overpre: Service pressure exceeded: pressure pushes back on the piston. Contents are retained.
hydraulic-status-state-read-only: Transfers paused: a connected pipe cannot read its saved data.
reciprocating-pump-status-state-read-onl: Pump paused to protect its saved contents.
reciprocating-pump-state-read-only: The pump cannot read its saved data. Pumping is paused to protect its contents.
block-placefailure-gearwright-reciprocat: The journal cannot accept this attachment.
The nearby pump and axle require different drive-shaft directions.
pipe-content-conflict: That change would join pipe networks containing different contents.
block-placefailure-gearwright-irrigator-: The Irrigator Pipe cannot be supported at that location.
hydraulic-status-flow-solving: Flow could not settle. Retrying shortly.
hydraulic-status-network-too-large: Flow paused: more than 4096 pipes and pump chambers are connected. Split them into smaller lines.
hydraulic-status-waiting-for-chunks: Waiting for the rest of the pipe route to load.
hydraulic-status-mixed-content: Connected pipes contain different contents; transfer is stopped.
hydraulic-status-mixed-sources: Different sources are trying to fill this empty network.
hydraulic-status-content-mismatch: A connected source or container has the wrong content.
hydraulic-status-gas-container-blocked: Steam cannot enter a Vintage Story liquid container.
hydraulic-status-invalid-content: The selected pipe content is unavailable.
hydraulic-status-no-source: No usable liquid container is connected.
hydraulic-status-reserve-reached: The old horizontal reserve has been reached.
hydraulic-status-deprecated: This Gravity Drain is deprecated; use a Copper Pipe Nozzle.
